sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 7 Status
sections.body:
- Devnet 7 is stable; dust has settled and network performing well
- Erigon onboarding in progress as the last client; Grandine was added before the weekend
  - Both Erigon and Grandine will have fewer validators until more deposits come in, so they may propose less frequently
- Prysm/Erigon combo missing slots on Dora; likely still syncing as full sync is being tested across all clients
- Death Star (modified Lodestar that acts maliciously) added to devnet 7 for chaos testing
- Malicious Prysm node updated by PandaOps; pending review from the "Aussies" before deployment
  - Will introduce more degrees of freedom than Death Star this week
- Plan is to increase chaos testing gradually on devnet 7 but not crash the network, since it was made available to a broader audience
- QUIC confirmed enabled on devnet 7

sections.heading: Devnet 8 and Devnet 9 Planning
sections.body:
- Devnet 8 targets spec cleanup changes (repricing EIPs Marius wants to do) and another fork transition test
- Timeline: next week or the week after; no rush given holidays and pending changes
  - Benchmarking still needs time before devnet 8 is ready
- Goal for devnet 8: smooth fork transition with all clients
- Devnet 9 envisioned as a non-finality/chaos-focused devnet, ideally within the next month
- Decision: devnet 8 to run discv5 only for EL (no discv4)
  - Besu confirmed support; Nimbus EL also supports and prefers this
  - Csaba to do a small code test to confirm before the devnet launch
- Suggestion to invite big application-level stakeholders (e.g., CowSwap, builders) to practice the fork transition on devnet 8

sections.heading: Fork Transition Bugs and Performance
sections.body:
- Main EL issues on devnet 7: gas accounting inconsistencies; nothing out of the ordinary
- CL surprise: SSZ stable containers at fork transition due to large validator set size (many exiting validators)
- Lodestar bug: spread operator used to pass Merkle node arguments blew the stack on large SSZ trees (hundreds of thousands of nodes)
  - Not caught in small-tree testing; only surfaced at devnet scale; now fixed
- Stable containers ~10-20% slower across clients compared to non-progressive implementation
  - Grandine confirmed significant slowdowns in some places; optimization needed
  - Teku confirmed slower implementation across the board; manageable but needs an optimization round before mainnet
  - Need to benchmark behavior with bigger data structures beyond basic benchmarking done so far

sections.heading: EIP Staging and SFI Status
sections.body:
- All devnet 7 EIPs appear to satisfy SFI criteria per [EIP-7723](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7723)
- PandaOps team comfortable with SFI move from testing perspective; EELS perspective also confirmed comfortable
- Agreement: SFI designation is an ACDE/ACDC decision; testing team and EL teams signal readiness on ACDT, formal ratification to happen at next ACD call Thursday
- EIP-7773 (Meta EIP for Glamsterdam upgrade): proposed move to Review status
  - No objections raised
  - Authors asked to add PRs to EIP editing office hours tomorrow for merge before Thursday's ACD call

sections.heading: BAL JSON RPC Alignment
sections.body:
- BAL-specific JSON RPC methods inconsistent across clients (error codes, empty lists vs. omitted fields, access list format)
- Toni created a HackMD summarizing all divergence points; clients asked to review
- Toni raised a PR against execution-APIs to clarify the points where clients diverge; target alignment by devnet 8
- Chase already working on a JSON RPC test suite; coordinating to add BAL/access list tests there makes sense
- Sub-call traces: question raised about adding gas reservoir and spilled gas fields to traces
  - Acknowledged as separate from BAL-specific JSON RPC alignment
  - Decision deferred to async discussion; clients to review and figure out approach

sections.heading: EIP-7997 Contracts Factory and EELS PR
sections.body:
- Toni created [EELS PR](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3198) to add EIP-7997 factory contract via irregular state transition
- Context: checking contract existence at fork boundary adds an entry to the execution witness, causing client divergence
  - Issue originally raised by Ignacio; [EIP PR](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11952/changes) (already merged) removed mention of irregular state transition from the EIP itself
  - EIP now says: if gas schedule makes normal deployment impossible, rely on irregular state transition, but does not specify one
- Toni discovered the issue while testing JSON RPCs: Erigon and Geth had different paths at the fork boundary because one deployed the factory and the other didn't
- Geth team (Marius): internal discussion concluded the check is unnecessary since the factory is already deployed on all relevant chains; no strong argument for specifying it
- Consensus: no need to specify irregular state transition; factory already exists in Genesis on mainnet and devnets
  - Checking existence adds unwanted witness entries
  - PR to be closed; no critical impact
  - Some minor cross-client differences may persist but considered acceptable
